summary.text: The counterexample is \(n=67\): the relevant residue sums are \(1+3+3+3+19+19+19=67\) for \(m=147\), and \(1+3+9\cdot7=67\) for \(m=2055\). Thus two distinct indices produce \(67\), so its multiplicity is at least \(2\), not \(1\).

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
A(m)=\sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor \log_2 m\rfloor}(m\bmod 2^k)
\]
be sequence A049802, where \(m\bmod 2^k\) denotes the least nonnegative residue of \(m\) modulo \(2^k\). Thus \(a(n)\), sequence A383327, is the number of indices \(m\) for which \(A(m)=n\).

We disprove the conjecture at the listed value \(n=67\) by exhibiting two distinct indices at which A049802 has value \(67\).

First take \(m=147\). Since
\[
2^7=128\le 147<256=2^8,
\]
we have \(\lfloor\log_2 147\rfloor=7\). Its residues modulo the relevant powers of two are
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccccc}
2^k&2&4&8&16&32&64&128\\ \hline
147\bmod 2^k&1&3&3&3&19&19&19.
\end{array}
\]
Indeed, \(147=144+3\), with \(144\) divisible by \(4,8,16\), while \(147=128+19\), with \(128\) divisible by \(32,64,128\). Therefore
\[
A(147)=1+3+3+3+19+19+19=67.
\]

Next take \(m=2055\). Since
\[
2^{11}=2048\le 2055<4096=2^{12},
\]
we have \(\lfloor\log_2 2055\rfloor=11\). Write
\[
2055=2048+7.
\]
Modulo \(2\), the residue is \(1\), and modulo \(4\), the residue is \(3\). For every \(k\) with \(3\le k\le 11\), the number \(2^k\) divides \(2048=2^{11}\), and \(0\le 7<2^k\). Hence
\[
2055\bmod 2^k=7\qquad(3\le k\le 11).
\]
There are nine integers \(k\) in the range \(3,4,\ldots,11\). Consequently,
\[
A(2055)=1+3+9\cdot 7=4+63=67.
\]

The two indices are distinct, since \(147\ne2055\). Thus the value \(67\) occurs in A049802 at least twice, namely at indices \(147\) and \(2055\). It follows directly that
\[
a(67)\ge 2,
\]
and therefore \(a(67)\ne1\).

Equivalently, if one uses the finite counting definition with the standard sufficient search range \(m<2^{n+1}\), both witnesses are included: indeed
\[
147<4096=2^{12}<2^{68},\qquad 2055<4096=2^{12}<2^{68}.
\]
Thus the filtered set used to define \(a(67)\) contains these two distinct elements and has cardinality at least two.

Finally, \(67\) belongs to the conjecture's set
\[
\{1,3,5,9,15,23,35,63,65,67\}.
\]
The conjecture asserts in particular that \(a(67)=1\), whereas the preceding calculation gives \(a(67)\ge2\). This contradiction disproves the conjecture.
